test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 30 Aug 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: For a healthy society, what should be the distribution of men and women in the population?

options.text: Equal number of men and women

solution:
The correct answer is__** equal number of men and women.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Human sex ratio is a measure used in anthropology and demography expressed as the** ratio of males to females in a population.**
 
• The sex ratio of humans, like other sexually active organisms, is approximately** 1:1**.
 
• In humans, the ratio of females to males at birth is somewhat skewed toward the male sex; This is estimated to be between** 1.03 and 1.06** men for every woman, or roughly 1.05 or 1.06.
 
• **Human sex **ratios have been studied more than any other species, and more data are accessible to humans than any other species, although understanding these data can be challenging.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• As of 2020, there are **108.18 **males for every** 100 **females in the total population of India.
 
• In India, there are** 662,903,415 or 662.90 million **females and 717,100,970 or 717.10 million males.
 
• Females constitute** 48.04** percent of the population compared to** 51.96 **percent of males. With **54.20 million** men, India has the highest proportion of men overall.
 
• In terms of ratio of women to men, India ranks 189th out of **201 countries **and territories. Among Asian countries, its ranking is **42nd **out of **51 countries **and territories.
